title: Member Bulletin: Internet-Wide Scanning for Exposed DICOM Services

content:
## TLP:GREEN - Alert level: Advisory

The following is shared with members on the basis of member-contributed reporting. Members report a marked increase in unsolicited connection attempts to DICOM service ports, consistent with internet-wide scanning for imaging systems reachable from outside the organisation.

## Observed activity

Perimeter telemetry from several members shows sustained connection attempts to standard DICOM ports from a rotating set of source addresses. In two cases the scanning identified genuinely reachable imaging services that had been exposed by a firewall change made for a research collaboration and never reverted.

## Recommended member actions

- Confirm that no DICOM service is reachable from outside the organisation's perimeter.
- Review firewall exceptions created for research or partner access and confirm each still has a current owner.
- Enable Application Entity title allowlisting on imaging services that must accept external associations.
- Alert on inbound connection attempts to imaging ports at the perimeter, which should be zero.

## Notes on this reporting

- Both confirmed exposures originated from temporary research access that was never withdrawn.
- Perimeter connection attempts to imaging ports have no legitimate baseline, so any volume is actionable.
- Application Entity allowlisting is available on most imaging platforms and is rarely enabled.
